docs.title: mlip
docs.text: Minimal, MLIP‑first workflows for molecular simulation. The goal is to keep setup and execution predictable while surfacing the ML interatomic potential (MLIP) runs front‑and‑center.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate mlip
pip install -e .
mlip --help

docs.title: Typical Flow
docs.text:
1. prep — build the solvated system with AmberTools/tleap
  2. mdequil — equilibrate with classical force field (optional)
  3. salt — adjust ions / hydroxide (optional)
  4. orb-prep — prepare ORB runs
  5. orb-submit — submit ORB runs to Slurm
  6. plumed-cv — write plumed.dat in per-run CV dirs (optional)

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• MLIP runs are the center of the workflow; prep exists to make them reliable.
  • Each command is YAML‑driven and writes outputs under systems/<system>/<prefix>_<buffer>/.
  • mlip is independent from qmmd and shares no runtime linkage.

docs.title: hbond
docs.text:
Hydrogen‑bond time‑series and lifetime analysis with cpptraj.

mlip hbond configs/<molecule>/analysis/hbond.yaml

docs.title: radgyr
docs.text:
Radius of gyration time‑series analysis with cpptraj.

mlip radgyr configs/<molecule>/analysis/radgyr.yaml

docs.title: QM/MM snapshot preparation
docs.text:
Prepare non-periodic, spherical Amber snapshots for TeraChem's built-in OpenMM QM/MM driver.

PYTHONPATH=src python -m mlip.cli qmmm configs/osteocalcin/qmmm/qmmm.yaml

With the package installed, the equivalent command is mlip qmmm configs/osteocalcin/qmmm/qmmm.yaml.

The osteocalcin YAML treats the 10 ns production NetCDF as the mother run. It requires all 1000 saved frames to be present, then selects frames 1, 112, 223, 334, 445, 556, 667, 778, 889, and 1000. The check prevents a partially written trajectory from changing the meaning of stop: last.

Each snapshot is imaged around the five calcium ions and converted to a non-periodic 28 Å sphere containing the full dimer and all neutralizing sodium ions. The charge -4 singlet QM region contains all five calcium ions, the side chains of GLA 6, 10, 13, 44, 48, and 51, ASP 19 and 57, and every water oxygen within 2.8 Å of a calcium. Coordinating OPC waters are converted to three-site TIP3P waters before their O/H atoms enter QM; their EP sites are removed. This gives 116-119 QM atoms in the sampled frames. Eight CA-CB boundaries are validated for TeraChem's automatic link atoms.

Each frame directory receives a carved system.parm7, frame.rst7, zero-based region.qm, tc.in, and a validation manifest. The terachem YAML mapping is written directly into tc.in, so the calculation type is selected through the input rather than a separate workflow.

For a single-point energy with pure spherical basis functions:

terachem:
  run: energy
  sphericalbasis: "yes"

For QM/MM molecular dynamics, retain run: md and place the MD controls under extra:

terachem:
  run: md
  seed_base: 20261026
  extra:
    nstep: 1000
    timestep: 0.5
    velocities: random
    tinit: 300.0
    thermostat: rescale
    mdbc: spherical
    md_density: 1.0

The packaged osteocalcin configuration retains the 500 fs MD setup for later use. The currently submitted calculation uses the single-point form above. TeraChem 25.03's embedded Amber reader only reads the Lennard-Jones A and B tables, however, so it ignores the C4 term during QM/MM. All five calcium ions are in the QM region, which reduces but does not eliminate the consequence for Ca interactions with MM water. After reviewing the manifests, run the generated calculations from the output directory with ./run_all.sh.

docs.title: salt
docs.text: Post‑equilibration system adjustment. Removes a counterion and converts the furthest water to hydroxide.
